name: George
imageCredit: Drawn by xanandra_. Painted by thetotalunknown2341
personality:
George is an odd piece of the puzzle that makes up Chroma Island. It seems like he’s the one in charge by his stance, his behavior, and the way he composes himself, but one simple interaction with him and Aeneas shows that he follows the terapagos fusion’s orders to an exact, with perhaps little to no personal decisions on major topics other than simply just. . . carrying out orders from Aeneas. 

What the exact relationship is between the two remains to be discovered, but the fact of the matter remains that George is a very capable guardian in all matters Aeneas has decided he should aid in, which is. . . basically everything, because Aeneas decided George should be a very very helpful person.

abilities.name: Ground
abilities.description: Can dig and move around underground. However, some surfaces will be too hard to break through.

abilities.name: Down to Earth
abilities.description: George can use Malignant Chain out of battle for the sole purpose of bringing an AFO (Annoying Flying Object) to the ground, or to stop cowards from running away from him.

abilities.name: Poison Puppeteer
abilities.description: If a pokemon is poisoned because of George they are also considered confused.

abilities.name: Shield Drill
abilities.description: Ignore raises in Defense and Sp. Defense.

moves.name: Fissure
moves.description: Has a really low chance [30%] to deal massive damage to the target.

moves.name: Acid Spray
moves.description: Reduces the target’s Sp. Defense by 2 stages.

moves.name: Heavy Slam
moves.description:
Damages, dealing more/less damage if George is/isn’t larger/heavier than his enemy. 
If the target has used minimize, bypass accuracy check and deal massive damage.

moves.name: Drill Run
moves.description: Damage with an increased critical hit ratio.

moves.name: Malignant Chain
moves.description: Damage with a chance [50%] to badly poison the target.

backstory:
To deny a choice, or to allow a choice?
To make that choice, or have someone else make it?
To determine their answer, or leave it up to them?

You.
Pecharunt.
Pecharunt, Pecharunt, Pecharunt, Pecharunt.

Haven’t you denied free will long enough?
How long will we keep this pointless game of control in check?

You created a garden of your own perfection. Every petal on every rose, a perfect representation of what you wanted.
A perfect mimicry of the most ideal, wonderful life. A life you could live forever.

what a joke you are to believe that.
how immature you are to believe that.

The flowers never listened to you.

Eyes closed and opened. Eyelids contacted flesh, bringing fluid to eyes. 
He didn’t want it to stop.
Why did it have to stop.
Why did it have to end.
It shouldn’t have ended.
Why.

The apple doesn’t fall far from the tree.
And there they were.
Someone frolickling across the meadow. 

Cheerful. Friendly.
Like a child going on an adventure.

“Let’s play a game!”
A game.

To deny a choice, or to allow a choice?
Allow.
To make that choice, or have someone else make it?
Someone else.
To determine their answer, or leave it up to them?
They should have the freedom to choose.

“Soo! If I’m the King of this Island….~~!!! Then you should be….??”
“. . . I suppose I should be the Royal Guard. . .?”
“Mmmm…!! Yeah!! That works!!! Great idea!!!!”

What a pathetic ending.
Are you still the leader of your fantasy? Or are you merely now a participant?
